issues.legal_issue: An appellate court should not remand an appeal merely because it considers some of the lower court’s reasoning erroneous when the available material enables it to decide the appeal.
material_facts: The appeal concerned an order granting a temporary injunction.
The High Court set aside the injunction and remitted the matter because it considered aspects of the trial court’s reasoning and factual foundation erroneous.
Documents and affidavits were available for the High Court to assess the prima facie case and decide whether to confirm, reverse or modify the injunction.
issues.conclusion: The remand was unnecessary; the appellate court should have decided the appeal on the material available, and a further remand was not warranted.
issues.legal_principle: In an appeal under Order 41 Rule 23 of the Code of Civil Procedure, a remand should not ordinarily be ordered merely because the appellate court disagrees with parts of the lower court’s reasoning. If the material is available, the appellate court should decide the appeal itself; unnecessary remands cause delay and prejudice. No earlier cases are cited for this principle.

predicates.appeal_from_temporary_injunction_order: The proceeding is an appeal from an order granting or refusing temporary injunctive relief.
predicates.remand_based_on_errors_in_reasoning: The appellate court remands because it considers some of the lower court’s reasoning or factual assessment erroneous.
predicates.material_for_appellate_decision_availabl: The material needed to decide the appeal is available to the appellate court.

issues.definition: When an appeal from a temporary injunction order is remanded for errors in reasoning despite sufficient material being available, the remand is not justified.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant with a sufficiently supported prima facie claim to possession may receive temporary protection against interference even when the validity of the competing agreements and the parties’ ultimate rights remain undecided.
material_facts: The claimant relied on agreements and payments and claimed possession of the land.
The owners supported the claimant’s account of possession, and several owners filed affidavits stating that the claimant was in possession.
A court commissioner’s report following physical verification recorded that the claimant was in possession.
The competing claimants produced copies of bills and receipts for construction materials, which the trial court found did not establish their possession.
The trial court treated the claimant’s possession as permissive and granted a temporary injunction without finally resolving the validity of the competing agreements or title.
issues.conclusion: The claimant had made out a prima facie case for temporary protection of possession. The temporary injunction was restored, with directions to maintain the status quo and not create third-party rights, construct on the land, or alter its nature pending the suit.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 39 Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure, a prima facie possessory claim supported by the available material may justify temporary injunctive protection. A possessory right may suffice for that interim relief without deciding the validity of agreements or the parties’ title. No earlier cases are cited for this principle.

predicates.temporary_injunction_proceeding: The proceeding seeks temporary protection against interference with a claimant’s possession.
predicates.claimant_possession_supported: The claimant’s possession is supported by material such as the opposing owners’ acknowledgments, affidavits, or a physical inspection report.
predicates.opposing_possession_not_established: The opposing claimants’ evidence does not establish that they possess the property.

issues.definition: If a temporary injunction proceeding concerns possession, the claimant’s possession is supported, and the opposing claimants’ possession is not established, the claimant receives temporary protection of possession.

issues.legal_issue: Findings about rights, title, or possession made when deciding temporary injunctive relief are tentative and do not determine the merits of the pending suit.
material_facts: The underlying suit remained pending and the parties had yet to lead evidence.
The Court restored temporary relief while expressly stating that findings about rights, title, and possession were tentative and subject to the trial court’s findings after evidence was led.
issues.conclusion: The findings supporting temporary relief remain tentative and are subject to determination at trial.
issues.legal_principle: Findings made at the interlocutory stage to decide temporary relief are provisional where the merits remain pending; they do not finally determine the parties’ rights, title, or possession. No provision or earlier case is cited for this express direction.

predicates.temporary_injunction_proceeding: The proceeding concerns temporary injunctive relief before final determination of the dispute.
predicates.merits_suit_pending: The underlying suit remains pending and the merits have not been finally determined.

issues.definition: When temporary relief is considered while the merits suit remains pending, findings made at that stage remain tentative.
